lawyer:
Mr. Fazlul Haque, Advocate ----- for the petitioner
Mr. Khijir Ahmed, Advocate ----- for the opposite party No. 1
parties:
Ishfaqul Fattah
Vs.
Md. Sujat Ali and others
full_judgment:
Abdul Awal, J:- Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 23.7.1998 passed by the learned District Judge, Sylhet, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 2 of 1996 under Section 64(2) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 arising out of Eviction Case No. 1 of 1996 under Section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 of the office of the deputy Commissioner, Sylhet, i.e. the opposite party No. 3, should not be set aside and or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts and circumstances under which the present petitioner has come before this Court,' in short, is that the Mutawalli of the Abdul Fattah and other Waqf Estate duly enrolled the Waqf in the Office of the Administrator of Waqf, Bangladesh, being E.C. Case No. 12886. While the father of the petitioner was the Mutawalli of the said Waqf Estate, he let out some residential accommodations and shops to different tenants and during his life time, he requested 4(four) tenants to vacate the houses being dilapidated in condition but they did not leave the houses. Subsequently, the petitioner being Mutwalli of the Waqf Estate also requested them time and again to vacate the houses for the purpose of construction and reconstruction of a market in the Waqf property on the ground of deteriorated condition of the houses and also to increase the income of the Waqf Estate but they did not pay any heed to his request. The petitioner, then, approached the Administrator of Waqf to evict the opposite party No. 1 and 3 others from the Waqf property by filing an application stating that the income of the Waqf property was Tk. 1995/- only which was a very meagre amount with which the expenses of the Waqf Estate could not be met and the repairing works of those houses were necessary. Permission for eviction and sale of some portion of Waqf property to raise fund for the construction of shops and residential accommodations was sought from the Administrator of Waqf. The Administrator of Waqf forwarded the said application to the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet, for eviction of the tenants from the Waqf property and the said application was registered as Eviction Case No. 1 of 1996. The usual notices, accordingly, were issued upon the opposite parties No. 1 and 3 others under Section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance giving them 30 days-time to vacate the house. Thereafter, the Deputy Commissioner, being opposite party no. 3 in the instant revision case, directed the Assistant Commissioner (Land); Sylhet, Sadar, to in-form him as to whether notice receiver has given up possession and also directed him to submit a sketch map of the land and its service return. The Assistant Commissioner (Land) visited the disputed Waqf property and there he found the occupants to whom the contents of notices were disclosed but they refused to receive the notices and thereby, the process server had to serve notices by hanging at the doors of their residences and submitted service return on 25.01.1996. The Tahsilder, Manucipal Land Office, also as per direction of the Deputy Commissioner-opposite party No. 3, went to the disputed Waqf property on 07.02.1996 and found the tenants living in 4 dilapidated houses and he also requested them to vacate the houses. 

 3. On receipt of the service return and the reports from the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Sadar, Sylhet, the opposite party No. 3 passed an order on 18.5.1996 in Eviction Case No. 1 of 1996 for the eviction of the opposite party No. 1 from the Waqf property and accordingly, the opposite party No. 1 was evicted on 22.5.1996 from the Waqf property through the law enforcing agencies under the supervision of a Magistrate. 

 4. Thereafter, the opposite party No. 1 filed an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 62 of 1996 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet, under Section 64(2) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962. After hearing both the parties and considering the materials on record learned District Judge, Sylhet, allowed the appeal setting aside the order of eviction. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order the petitioner preferred the instant Revision Case under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure before this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 8. Mr. Haque further submitted referring to section 64(1) of the Ordinance where it has been stated that even a co-sharer in Waqf property or a beneficiary or any other person interested in a Waqf who creates disturbance or obstruction in the peaceful management of the Waqf can be evicted from the Waqf property under the Ordinance. In the instant case the opposite party no. 1 does not even fall under section 2(8) of the Waqf Ordinance and as such he is regarded purely a trespasser according to Section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance. Therefore, the eviction of the opposite party No. 1 from the Waqf property was lawful. 

 "ACTION AGAINST TRESPASSERS AND MISCREANTS. (1) If a co-sharer in Waqf property or an individual beneficiary or any other person interested in a Waqf, or a stranger, creates disturbances or obstruction in the peaceful management of the Waqf or any institution attached thereto in any way, or disturbs the possession of a Waqf property by the mutawalli or any person or a managing committee appointed by the Administrator for managing the said property, or commits trespass on any such property, the Administrator shall apply to the Deputy Commissioner, who shall evict the trespasser, or take such steps for preventing such disturbance or obstruction as he deems  fit. 

 12. In view of above Section, the Deputy Commissioner is empowered not only to evict the trespasser but also the persons who, according to him, creates disturbance or obstruction to the peaceful management of the affairs of the Waqf property. Therefore, the view that the Deputy Commissioner is empowered only to evict only the trespasser is without any substance. In the instant case, the Deputy Commissioner ordered for the eviction of the petitioner from the Waqf property for smooth, efficient and peaceful management of the Waqf property. 

 14. In the definition of the Waqf Ordinance, there is no word like 'trespassers' and `miscreants' as are found in Section 64 of the Waqf Ordinance. This indicates that the persons who are not governed under the definition of Section 2(8) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 are all regarded either as strangers or trespassers or miscreants. The opposite party No. 1 being not converted by Section 2(8) of the said Ordinance falls under the category of stranger or trespasser or miscreant. 

 16. The finding of the learned District Judge that the opposite party no. 1 was neither a person interested in Waqf nor a stranger but was a tenant and as such Section 64(1) of the Ordinance has no manner of application in case of opposite party No. 1 and that no opportunity was given to him of being heard are misconceived and erroneous. Since the opposite party No. V being not covered by Section 2(8) of Waqf Ordinance his eviction from the Waqf property is found to be justified and legal. Even the person falls under the category of Section 2(8) of the Waqf Ordinance can be evicted by the Deputy Commissioner if he considers that he creates disturbance or obstruction in the peaceful management of the Waqf property. 

 In view of the discussions made above and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to interfere with the impugned judgment and order. 

 18. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 23.7.1998 passed by the learned District Judge in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 62 of 1996 is set aside. The order of stay granted earlier stands vacated.
